title: Pulse Inspector: compact correlation-driven trace drilldown
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, correlation-id–first trace drilldown called 'Pulse Inspector' that surfaces a lightweight view of a request's timeline, span minimap, and contextual filters inside the Redwood Console. The goal is a fast-to-open panel that helps engineers quickly triage latency spikes and error clusters without leaving the main dashboard. Pulse Inspector should complement the full Trace Explorer (deep dive) and act as the default entry point from dashboards, alerts, and rollout incident cards.
acceptance_criteria: Panel opens from dashboard or alert in under 250ms (perceived) with a skeleton then progressive hydration
Correlation ID banner shows copyable ID, link to full trace, and breadcrumbs to parent resources
Timeline scrubbing with span highlighting and a minimap that indicates concentration of spans/errors
Quick filter builder (service, span.kind, status, tag) that applies to both timeline and span list
Lightweight span inspector exposes key attributes (duration, start offset, tags) and a 'Jump to logs' action
Keyboard accessibility for open/close (k), next/previous span (j/k), and filter focus (f)
Design passes PM review and usability test with 6 engineers (task completion rate >= 90%)
decisions: Use an overlay panel anchored to the right of the console rather than a full-page modal to preserve dashboard context
Show a condensed span minimap instead of a full waterfall to reduce cognitive load for quick triage
Support progressive loading: initial header + minimap + top 5 spans, then lazy-load full span list and tags
Expose primary actions (Copy ID, Open full trace, Open logs) and hide advanced inspection behind 'Expand'
engineering_requirements: API: endpoint to fetch trace summary by correlation id with span aggregates and error buckets
Backend: precomputed span density per 100ms bucket for minimap visualization
Backend: tags and top-k span attributes included in initial payload to avoid extra round trips
Frontend: skeleton states + staggered hydration for perceived performance
Telemetry: events for panel open, copy-id, open-full-trace, and quick-filter usage
usability_notes: Primary persona: platform engineers triaging rollout regressions and incident responders
Prefer short affordances (5-7 tokens) in filter chips to keep visual density low
Color strategy: use alert red for error density in minimap, orange for p95/latency buckets
Mobile: panel should degrade to a full-screen swipable modal on narrow viewports
